we have presented a novel neural network architecture that operates on graph-structured inputs, leveraging masked selfattentional layers to learn different weights for each node in a neighborhood.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to previous approaches based on convolutional neural networks, attention mechanisms are well-suited to capture the graph dependencies of a given task.
attention mechanisms can be a viable alternative to graph convolutions in graph-based semi-supervised learning, with a more principled approach to neighborhood aggregation.
, by using attention mechanisms, we can achieve state-of-the-art performance in semi-supervised classification of graphs without relying on handcrafted topological or spectral features.
